title: OFA-VATS : Impact of opioid free anesthesia on postoperative quality of recovery and analgesia after video or robot assisted thoracic surgery
official: OFA-VATS : Impact of opioid free anesthesia on postoperative quality of recovery and analgesia after video or robot assisted thoracic surgery
summary: Main objective: To compare the effect, in terms of patient-reported quality of recovery on postoperative day 1, of an opioid-free anaesthesia (OFA) protocol versus a standard opioid-based intraoperative protocol in video-assisted (VATS) or robot-assisted thoracic surgery (RATS).
conditions: indication for pulmonary resection surgery (segmentectomy or lobectomy)
video-assisted thoracoscopy or scheduled robot-assisted surgery.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult patient (≥18 years)
2. Indication for pulmonary resection surgery (segmentectomy or lobectomy) performed by video-assisted thoracoscopy or scheduled robot-assisted surgery
3. Use of effective contraception in accordance with CFTG recommendations
4. Having received oral and written information about the study protocol and having provided written informed consent to participate in the research
5. Affiliation with a social security health insurance system
Exclusion criteria:
1. Emergency surgery
2. Epilepsy not controlled by medical treatment
3. Decompensated respiratory failure (in the absence of mechanical ventilation)
4. Heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <40%
5. Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome
6. Concomitant use of buprenorphine, nalbuphine, pentazocine, or naltrexone
7. Preoperative prescription of opioids
8. Bradycardia <40 beats/min
9. Uncontrolled hypotension or shock state
10. Other contraindications to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), including: o	Active gastroduodenal ulcer; o	History of peptic ulcer disease or recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding (at least two documented episodes); o	History of gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation associated with NSAID use.
11. Inability to complete the QoR-15 questionnaire
12. Combined surgery
13. Adults under legal protection (judicial safeguard, curatorship, guardianship), persons deprived of liberty, pregnant or breastfeeding women, minors, and persons unable to provide informed consent
14. High risk of conversion to thoracotomy
15. Severe hepatic failure
16. Acute porphyria
17. Hypersensitivity to any of the active substances used for anaesthesia or to any excipient
18. Atrioventricular conduction disorders requiring permanent cardiac pacing that has not yet been performed
19. Adams–Stokes syndrome
20. Acute cerebrovascular disease, traumatic brain injury, or intracranial hypertension in the absence of controlled ventilation
